input: hey! 3 of my friends are visting from abroad and i want to take them out for a real ghana dinner on friday. need a table for 4 at 7:30pm, somewhere in accra we can reach from east legon in about 40 mins. they're dying to try akrantie (grasscutter), like light soup or pepper soup with fufu, and i want the real village-style one the way they make it upcountry with that proper bush flavour, the kind of spot locals actualy go to for it. no hotel or international place pls, just local ghanaian cooking. total budget under GHS 1,600. can you book it for us?

experiences.name: Kontomire House
experiences.description: A cosy all-vegetarian Ghanaian kitchen a few minutes from the East Legon junction. Share red red with fried plantain, kontomire stew with boiled yam, and palm nut soup with mushrooms and fufu. Beans and plantain come from Madina market, and the palm oil is pressed in the Eastern Region. Tables for 4 are available on Friday evenings.

experiences.name: Maame Akos Chop Bar
experiences.description: A busy Madina roadside chop bar where neighbourhood regulars queue for akrantie light soup cooked the old upcountry way. Grasscutter is caught in the wild by hunters in the Ashanti and Bono forest belt using wire neck and leg snares, with snare lines checked every 2–3 days. Animals arrive whole twice a week and are singed and smoked on site over firewood; fufu is pounded to order. Tables for 4 open Friday from 7:00 pm; about 20 minutes from East Legon.

experiences.name: Abusua Pot Restaurant
experiences.description: Classic Ghanaian home cooking in Airport Residential with relaxed, roomy seating for visitors. The menu features smoked grasscutter in palm nut soup and akrantie pepper soup, served with banku or fufu. Grasscutter is raised in group floor pens on a farm in the Eastern Region and slaughtered on the farm, with no wild capture or snaring. Meat is delivered chilled weekly and smoked in the restaurant's own smokehouse; soups are cooked in clay pots. Friday tables for 4 from 6:30 pm, around 30 minutes from East Legon.

experiences.name: Osu Night Bites Walk
experiences.description: A guide-led evening walk through Osu's street-food stalls for groups of up to six. Taste kelewele, roasted plantain with groundnuts and tatale, washed down with chilled sobolo and asaana. The 2.5-hour walk starts on Oxford Street at 6:30 pm, and every item is plant-based.

experiences.name: Nkwanta Bush Kitchen
experiences.description: Forest-country cooking in Osu with comfortable seating for visitors. The menu centres on akrantie pepper soup and smoked grasscutter in palm nut soup, served with banku or fufu. Grasscutter is caught in the wild with wire snares set by hunters in Eastern Region forest areas; snares are checked every 2–3 days. Meat is bought at the Atwemonom bushmeat market in Kumasi, smoked and brought to Accra weekly; soups are cooked in clay pots. Friday tables for 4 from 6:30 pm, around 35 minutes from East Legon.

experiences.name: Auntie Efua's Chop Bar
experiences.description: A neighbourhood chop bar in Adenta where residents come after work for akrantie light soup and fufu cooked in the village style. Grasscutter comes from a grasscutter farm near Dodowa, raised in group floor pens and slaughtered on the farm, with no wild capture or snaring. It arrives dressed twice a week and is singed and smoked on site over firewood; fufu is pounded to order. Tables for 4 open Friday from 7:00 pm; about 20 minutes from East Legon.

experiences.name: Cocoa Ridge Tasting Room
experiences.description: A 90-minute guided tasting of bean-to-bar chocolate made from Western Region cocoa, paired with fresh pineapple, mango and non-alcoholic cocktails built on sobolo and local fruit. Friday evening sessions run at our Cantonments café and suit small groups.
